page.layout: One column of verse, full width, under a heading line at the top. Below the verse, a rule and a printed ornament (not text).

l.i: Sicut apis, saltus, hortosq; & olentia nata
Pascua, per flores & thyma summa volat:
Actore[?] hinc carpit, summo tenus optima quaq;
Et dulcis fingit nobile mellis opus:
Sic per Musarum, Tempeq; & amœna vireta
Bilstenius[?] volitans, optima quaq; legit.
Atq; hinc gignit opus, genitumq; exponit in auras,
Forsitan hoc Solis lucida tela fugit?
Nil minus: ingenua nam totum continet orbem
Doctrina, & multis eruta sensa libris.
Non in aperto igitur passim prostare veretur,
Serviat ut studiis, Grex studiosa, tuis.
Hoc lege, sed lectum, bene percipe, pectore conde:
Hoc exprome usu, cum feret usus, opus.
Nec vero hoc satis est: plus ultra, Symbolon esto
(Dum contacta tibi ex ultima meta) tuum.
Post ea quæ Sophiæ Proceres monumenta dedere,
Illa leges oculis, illa teres manibus.
Virtutis sectare viam: comitabitur illam,
Ingredere, labor: progrediaris, amor.
Emenso continget honor, pulcerrima merces
Ergo age, virtutis perfice gnauus iter.

page.notes: The ornament below the rule is a printer's ornament, not text. Doubtful readings: "Actore" (first letters possibly a ct ligature, perhaps "Ab ore"), and "Bilstenius" (the long s may be misread). The ligature ct is copied as plain ct. Printed spelling and abbreviations (-que as q;) are kept as they stand.
